A **paired samples t-test** is used to test whether the **mean difference** between two **related measurements** is different from zero.[1][2] It is appropriate when the same subjects are measured twice, or when observations are matched into pairs, such as *before vs. after* measurements.[2][3][8]

- **What it tests:** whether the average of the pairwise differences is \(0\).[1][6][7]
- **When to use it:** when the two samples are **dependent/related**, not independent.[2][3][9]
- **Key assumption:** the **differences** between pairs are approximately normally distributed.[1][2][3][8]
- **How it works:** compute each pair’s difference, then run a one-sample \(t\)-test on those differences against \(0\).[1][2][6]
- **Degrees of freedom:** \(n - 1\), where \(n\) is the number of pairs.[2][6]

If you want, I can also show:
- the **formula**,
- a **worked example**,
- or how to do it in **R / Python / SPSS**.
